voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: THE SERIES INTRODUCTION (a reel posted before episode 1; pipeline number 98, never a story episode). It says what the series is and makes only checkable claims: the traditional count of the Mahabharata is a hundred thousand verses (the epic's own 'shatasahasri samhita'; stated as tradition's count); the text followed is the Critical Edition (Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune); material from later tradition is tagged on screen ('As tradition tells it', as in episode 14); the voices are Kokoro text-to-speech and every frame is drawn in code; the telling begins with Sauti before the sages at Naimisha (CE Adi 1.1). The montage shows images from episodes already made: Janamejaya's snake sacrifice (CE 1.47-53), Garuda storming heaven (1.28), Bhrigu's curse on Agni (1.6-7), Satyavati the ferry girl on the Yamuna (1.57), Vyasa's arrival at the sacrifice (1.54); the dice and the war are named only as far ahead (summarised in 1.55). No channel name, date or episode count is stated.
structure: HOOK (the title as a statement, <= 3 s) -> the promise (the count, the plan) -> a montage of six images -> THE TURN after a real silence (the vow: shorten, never change; the close-up) -> the method (the critical edition, the tradition label, synthetic voices, drawn in code) -> a second silence -> where it begins (Sauti at Naimisha) -> the invitation, with the source line and episode 1's title; the last shot keeps drifting.

strings.sourceLine: Text: the Mahabharata · BORI Critical Edition

lines.text: The Mahabharata. As Vyasa told it.
lines.say: The Mahabharata. [p:120] As Vyasa told it.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a title as a statement): the great fire fills the frame and a push goes into it; lines of gold verse rise out of the flame. The words as a card low in the frame; then the series title.

lines.text: Tradition counts a hundred thousand verses.
lines.note: THE SIGNATURE SHOT: a crane up from the fire's sparks into a lapis night where the verses lie in rows of gold to the horizon, a land of lights, flowing toward us.

lines.text: I will tell it start to finish, one short episode at a time.
lines.note: A green dusk: a path of small lamps winds to the horizon; they light one by one, near to far, as the camera tracks along it.

lines.text: A sacrifice that drags serpents into the fire.
lines.note: MONTAGE 1 (CE 1.47-53): the king's hall in teal night, the fire high; serpents fall out of the dark toward it; a tilt down with them.
MONTAGE 2 (CE 1.28): Garuda, blazing gold, large in a storm sky, wings opening; an orbit.

lines.text: A sage who curses fire itself.
lines.note: MONTAGE 3 (CE 1.6-7): Bhrigu, close, in crimson; the arm thrown forward on 'curses'.

lines.text: A ferry girl on the Yamuna.
lines.note: MONTAGE 4 (CE 1.57): Satyavati rowing her boat across the deep-blue river; a lateral track.

lines.text: The poet, walking into his own story.
lines.note: MONTAGE 5 (CE 1.54): through a carved arch, Vyasa walks up the lamp-lit hall in his own gold light.

lines.text: And far ahead: the dice, and the war.
lines.note: MONTAGE 6 (a far promise, CE 1.55): from above, two dice fall on a red cloth; on 'the war' the cloth's grid becomes a field and two lines of small spearmen face each other in iron light. A pull back.

lines.text: I will shorten it. I will never change it.
lines.say: I will shorten it. [p:300] I will never change it.
lines.note: THE TURN, after a real silence: the close-up. Vyasa's face against a pearl dawn: weary, then resolved, then a small warmth; his eyes come to us.

lines.text: I follow the critical edition. What comes from later tradition, I label.
lines.say: I follow the critical edition. [p:200] What comes from later tradition, [p:80] I label.
lines.note: Palm leaves of the text on ivory; a plaque names the edition; on 'label' the series' own tag stamps onto one leaf: As tradition tells it.

lines.text: The voices are synthetic. Every frame is drawn in code.
lines.say: The voices are synthetic. [p:200] Every frame is drawn in code.
lines.note: A shot builds itself in the open: sky, hills, trees, the hut and a figure arrive plane by plane as bare shapes, then the light and colour come on. Two small tags say what is synthetic.

lines.text: It begins with Sauti, a storyteller, before the sages of Naimisha.
lines.say: It begins with Sauti, [p:80] a storyteller, [p:80] before the sages of Naimisha.
lines.note: After a second silence: the forest at the blue hour, a small fire, the seated sages; Sauti comes in with his staff. A crane down through the trees.

lines.text: Follow, and meet me at the fire for episode one.
lines.say: Follow, [p:150] and meet me at the fire [p:60] for episode one.
lines.note: The same fire at first light: Sauti seated, a hand open to us; the source line (fixed), then 'Episode 1: The Storyteller Arrives'. The shot keeps drifting to the last frame.
